niche_preference_profile: This user prefers interfaces with strong, intentional visual mood and clear structure. They often favor dark, immersive, high-contrast or monochrome presentations when paired with refined focus, layered depth, and sleek styling, but they also respond positively to bright light themes when those layouts are cleaner, more spacious, and better organized than the alternative. Across examples, they consistently like clear hierarchy, obvious selection states, modular card-based organization, rounded but controlled shapes, and interfaces that feel polished rather than plain. They tend to prefer either compact, efficient layouts with strong grouping or sparse layouts with deliberate focus, while rejecting clutter, weak hierarchy, flatness, and ambiguous controls.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers a deliberate, stylized color system with a strong mood—most often dark, immersive, high-contrast, neon-accented, or monochrome palettes, though also likes bright light themes when they create a cleaner and more organized experience than the alternative.
Prefers strong hierarchy and focal clarity: clear sectioning, dominant hero elements, emphasized headings, stronger modal isolation, and layouts that guide attention cleanly.
Prefers intentional spacing and density—either compact, efficiently grouped layouts or sparse, focused compositions—while rejecting cluttered, awkwardly segmented, or visually heavy arrangements.
Prefers modular, card-based organization with distinct grouped content, often favoring multiple compact panels over monolithic blocks and clearer option presentation over vague minimal controls.
Prefers rounded geometry, usually soft or moderately rounded corners on cards, inputs, containers, and controls, while avoiding shapes that feel too sharp or, in one case, overly puffy.

Prefers polished, integrated controls and inputs: compact buttons, refined secondary actions, filled or softly contrasted fields, subtle icon buttons, and cleaner control treatments with stronger affordance.

Prefers interfaces that make options, states, and data explicit—such as descriptive cards, visible metrics, highlighted selections, and richer contextual detail—rather than ambiguous or under-explained UI.
